title: NovaHelix POC kickoff - traffic tail, concurrency & benchmarking
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC to validate tail latency and concurrency behavior for NovaHelixs recommendation inference. Agreed to reproducible benchmarks using workload replay and token distributions; primary success criteria are 99th percentile latency under 350ms at defined QPS bursts, and cost per 1M tokens within target. Next steps: exchange benchmark template, schedule load-replay run, share security checklist and SSO details.
action_items: Avery Chen: send POC pricing sheet + benchmark template; due 2027-06-11
Diego Martinez: prepare synthetic replay scripts and sample token histograms; due 2027-06-14
Priya Singh: provide 2 weeks of production traces (anonymized) and expected QPS windows; due 2027-06-12
Marco Ruiz: confirm network egress constraints and VPC peering windows for private test; due 2027-06-15
Elena Park: validate SSO requirements and provide SAML metadata; due 2027-06-13
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark template and security questionnaire
Customer to upload anonymized traces to shared S3 link
Schedule replay run: target week of 2027-06-21
Plan 1-hour deep-dive on quantization/latency tradeoffs after initial replay
meeting_header: Date: 2027-06-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 min | Location: Zoom
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood Inference, Im the account owner on this. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Priya Singh: Priya here, Head of ML at NovaHelix.
[00:10] Marco Ruiz: Marco, Platform.
[00:12] Elena Park: Elena, SRE.
[00:15] Diego Martinez: Diego from Redwood, I'll be supporting the POC execution and benchmarks.
[00:20] Avery Chen: Cool. High level goal -- we want to validate that Redwood can meet NovaHelixs tail latency needs under bursty QPS shape, and that we can size Dedicated or Private correctly for cost predictability. Priya, can you give us the production context?
[00:33] Priya Singh: Yeah so currently we're running a recommender that powers in-app suggestions, peak QPS is around 180 qps for a 10 minute window during campaigns, but typical baseline is more like 20 qps. Tokens per request vary a lot, input avg ~120 tokens, output avg ~45 but the tail spikes to like 600 tokens when we include user history.
[00:54] Marco Ruiz: And we have hard reqs on P99 latency -- if campaign traffic goes high we need 95% of requests under 200ms and P99 under 350ms. Also cost target for inference is roughly $12 per 1M tokens processed, otherwise it's hard to justify.
[01:12] Diego Martinez: OK thats helpful. A couple clarifying qs: when you say 180 qps peak, is that sustained for the 10 minutes always or sometimes it bursts higher for short seconds-level spikes?
[01:25] Priya Singh: Mostly sustained across that 10 min window, but we see microbursts up to 350 qps for 20-30s when an influencer post goes viral.
[01:36] Avery Chen: Good, so we need to model both sustained and microbursts. For the POC we typically ask for a two-pronged replay: 1) a 10-minute sustained window to validate throughput and warm cache behavior, and 2) a synthetic microburst test to stress tail and autoscaling. We'll also want per-request token histograms so we can model KV cache and batching efficiency.
[01:58] Elena Park: Quick security check: we need SOC2 Type II evidence, SAML SSO, and KMS integration. Were evaluating private deployment but want to see hosted performance first. Also retention policies, logs -- audit trail is mandatory.
[02:15] Avery Chen: We can share SOC2 artifacts and our security questionnaire. For KMS, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys, and we provide audit logs in console with token-level anonymization. We'll attach docs.
[02:30] Marco Ruiz: Network-wise, if we do Private in our VPC we need peering windows and an egress lock down. For hosted, our security team will want to see TLS and mutual auth.
[02:41] Diego Martinez: Noted. Back to workload sizing -- can you share the token distribution? You said avg input 120, output 45, tail up to 600. Do you have percentiles?
[02:53] Priya Singh: We have 50th/90th/99th: input 90/240/560, output 30/120/400. But those 99th's are low volume but they impact memory/KV and p99 lat.
[03:09] Diego Martinez: Great. For benchmark design we'll ask for a replay CSV with timestamp, model variant, input tokens, output tokens, and a sample of headers for auth routing. We'll run both hosted and Dedicated configs to compare. For p99 latency, we will instrument with tracing and capture token-level times.
[03:31] Priya Singh: How do you account for cold KV cache effects? Our production sees a compounding slowdown for new sessions.
[03:40] Diego Martinez: Well do two-phase runs: cold start windows and warm steady-state. For cold we purge caches and ramp to load; for warm we'll seed KV caches using a prefix replay prior to peak. That will let us measure realistic tails.
[03:54] Avery Chen: Also we'll capture batching stats and effective tokens per batch to show cost extrapolation. Important for your cost target.
[04:03] Marco Ruiz: Regarding models, we're evaluating two open models: a smaller 13B quantized and a 33B float variant. Were concerned about quantization-induced quality regressions. Can Redwood run both in the POC?
[04:16] Diego Martinez: Yes, we can host multiple variants and do A/B comparisons. For quantization quality we'll run your eval set and compute rouge/semantic and human review on a sample. We usually recommend a quantized variant for Dedicated unless p99 constraints push you to larger instance types.
[04:33] Priya Singh: Timeline question: wed like to be able to decide Dedicated vs hosted by mid July. Is that feasible?
[04:39] Avery Chen: Feasible. Proposed POC timeline: week 1 (this week) exchange traces and security docs; week 2 Redwood runs initial replay in hosted and shares baseline; week 3 run microburst and cold-start tests and analyze; week 4 customer review and decision. Thats about 3-4 weeks, fits mid-July decision.
[04:58] Elena Park: What about SLA targets during the POC? We dont expect production SLA but want baseline SLOs for measurement.
[05:05] Diego Martinez: We publish SLO measurements but for POC we'll set measurement SLOs: target p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms under the sustained 180 qps, and for microbursts well capture tails and provide mitigation options like autoscale buffer or route fallback to smaller model tuned for latency.
[05:28] Priya Singh: If you need to fall back to smaller model during microburst, how do you measure quality impact?
[05:34] Diego Martinez: We'll run the eval prompt set and compute delta on our quality metrics plus surface a set of user-visible diffs. Also you can configure a percent-based A/B so only X% get the fallback during a campaign while we monitor live quality.
[05:49] Marco Ruiz: Cost math: at our expected mix we estimate ~1.8B tokens per month. So cost per 1M tokens target $12 would mean monthly cost ~ $21.6k, which we need to compare vs infra + engineer ops. Can you produce a cost projection for hosted vs Dedicated?
[06:06] Avery Chen: Yes we'll provide a projection sheet showing effective tokens per second, batching gains, and estimated unit costs for hosted and Dedicated with reserved capacity. Well show sensitivity to average tokens and tail frequency.
[06:18] Priya Singh: For the replay, we need guidance on how to sanitize user PII before sharing traces.
[06:25] Diego Martinez: We'll share a sanitization script; typically you replace user IDs with hashed tokens and strip free-text fields. For our telemetry needs we only need token counts, timestamps, and request/response lengths.
[06:37] Elena Park: On observability, can Redwood provide request-level tracing and token-level cost so our billing team can reconcile?
[06:44] Diego Martinez: Yes, Console gives per-route, per-token breakdown and trace-export in JSON; we can also add custom tags for your internal IDs.
[06:52] Priya Singh: How much effort is required to run the replay from our side? Our infra team is slammed right now.
[06:58] Avery Chen: We can run the replay if you provide S3 traces and credentials; otherwise we can give a lightweight Docker replay runner your team can run. For private deployment there are extra networking steps.
[07:10] Marco Ruiz: If we do hosted first, will the observed latency translate to private? We're worried about network hops to Redwood hosted endpoints.
[07:19] Diego Martinez: Network-to-hosted adds ~10-30ms depending on region. For Private in your VPC you'll eliminate that network hop but the infra sizing is what really changes tail; we can model that. During POC we'll run hosted and, if desired, a smoke Private run with limited capacity to compare.
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts, speaker overlaps, and some product name mis-hearings. Customer is particularly focused on p99 latency under bursty traffic, token distribution extremes, and security/KMS requirements.
questions: What are the exact percentiles for token lengths across 30, 60, 90 days?
Does NovaHelix have a preferred model family or do you want Redwood recommendations?
Confirm expected decision date for Dedicated vs hosted?
